answer: No. Exactly three current official SGLang candidates were inspected. The grouped-quant kernel bypasses Gemma 4's whole-row dynamic-FP8 path, HPC-Ops attention rejects Gemma 4's d256/d512 sliding-window geometry, and the selected prefill-graph padding guard is absent from the locked v0.5.13 runtime and exact launch. The selected upstream consumer was executed offline from its exact AST, but it can remove zero work from the locked request.

decision_contract.claim_tested: A current official runtime or kernel change exposes one nonduplicate source-complete mechanism that can remove work from the locked Gemma 4 31B c32 producer-to-consumer path without a generic runtime replacement.
decision_contract.falsifier: All three bounded candidates either fail the exact producer/geometry contract or require a runtime path absent from the locked source and launch, making their exact activated work zero.

primary_sources.reason: The merged source routes group_size == x.shape[-1] directly to sglang_per_token_quant_fp8. The exact dense Gemma 4 dynamic-FP8 activation path is whole-row, so the new group kernel is not invoked. The PR's reported B200 grouped/EP-MoE gains do not transfer to H200 or this producer.

The backend requires head_dim 128, page size 64, and no sliding window. Exact Gemma 4 uses d256 local attention, d512 global attention, page size 1, and 50 sliding-window layers. Its FP8 fused producer is wired only for Hunyuan V3. The PR also reports H200 regressions for 4K Qwen c32 and does not support Gemma's geometry.

The exact upstream can_run_graph method was compiled from the selected source AST and reproduced the 2x padding decision. The locked v0.5.13 tree has neither this runner nor cuda_graph_config.py, and the exact launch has only the legacy decode --cuda-graph-max-bs argument. Activating it would require the excluded generic runtime replacement.

first_decision_bearing_consumer.decision: Reject graph replay when padded_num_tokens > 2 * num_tokens; otherwise allow graph replay.

requirements: The eager fallback consumes the same raw ForwardBatch and produces the same logits semantics as graph replay.
The guard changes only graph eligibility; it does not change token IDs, positions, KV ownership, attention geometry, quantization, or model weights.
At the 2x boundary graph replay remains eligible; above 2x it is rejected.
A locked-runtime claim requires the real pinned producer to call this consumer; a source method present only after a runtime rebase receives zero credit.
